source_only_findings_not_candidate_label.fact: UnmarshalText is a receiver method; errors are NumError causes, syntax/bits assign zero and range assigns uint64 maximum. Three pairwise distinct error states is contradicted; two state classes is supported.

Parse creates a fresh local ByteSize, invokes UnmarshalText and returns value/error. It has no caller receiver. Uncalled wrapper status does not obscure this source fact; arbitrary caller adaptation remains unknown.
MustParse is a function, panics on Parse error, and returns only the successful value. Parse's zero/max local states are not returned as error-state values from MustParse.

Encoder declares a custom field callback interface. No concrete traversal/order/empty/nesting behavior is implemented by this declaration. Missing callback evidence is not an automatic negative label.

Exported nonignored primitive fields with default sequence options retain repeated value order; empty slices are omitted, scalar empty strings remain unless omitempty, named nesting uses bracket scopes. Delimiter/numbered options and custom encoders override this; anonymous structs can flatten. Original broad absent-vs-empty wording is not an unconditional universal guarantee.
valueString returns one formatted string. Aggregation, omission and bracket-key construction occur in its caller. A composed adapter is not equivalent to selecting this helper alone.
Lexer.Next emits one word, skips comments and returns an empty string on tokenizer error. It does not return the previously completed token list. Caller loops are separate compositions.
Tokenizer.Next returns one typed token; quote/escape EOF returns the current unfinished token and error, not the accumulated completed prefix.

Split constructs the default lexer, appends successful words only, returns completed words with a later quote/escape error, and starts with a nonnil empty slice. This directly supports the stated string-split scope; full POSIX substitution/Reader-fault proof is not required.
